name: Viracocha
role: Creator and culture bringer who rose from Lake Titicaca
fun_fact: The name Viracocha was also used by Andean people for the Spaniards, who were first mistaken for returning creators.

name: Pachamama
role: Living earth mother who receives offerings and gives life
fun_fact: Before drinking, many people in the Andes pour a few drops on the ground for Pachamama, a small daily act of thanks.

name: Inti
role: Sun god and divine ancestor of the Inka kings
fun_fact: The Inka ruler was called the child of the sun, and the great sun temple in Cusco was lined with gold.

name: Manco Capac
role: Founder of Cusco and first Inka king
fun_fact: The golden staff he carried was said to sink into the earth at the exact spot where Cusco would be built.

name: Mama Ocllo
role: Sister and wife of Manco Capac, teacher of weaving
fun_fact: She is remembered as the one who taught Andean women to spin and weave, skills that carried both wealth and sacred meaning.

name: Ai Apaec
role: Fanged Moche being shown with a knife and a severed head
fun_fact: His name is a later label, and scholars still argue whether he was one god, several, or a role played by a priest.

name: Inkarrí
role: Inka king whose severed head grows a new body underground
fun_fact: In the Quechua stories his body grows bone by bone, and when it is complete the world will turn over.

name: Fox
role: Cunning Andean trickster who tries to reach the moon
symbols: the dark marks on the moon
fun_fact: Andean storytellers have long pointed to the dark patches on the moon and called them the fox who climbed too high.

name: Apu
role: Mountain lord and guardian of a particular territory
fun_fact: Each apu has a personal name, and pilgrims still climb to high passes to greet the greatest peaks with offerings.

name: Mama Quilla
role: Moon goddess, sister and wife of the sun
fun_fact: Inka priests tracked her phases to set festivals, and an eclipse was read as a sign that she was troubled.
